To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 37·5 kb region of yeast chromosome XI includes the SME1 gene, which encodes a protein kinase involved in meiosis, the MEF2, which encodes an elongation factor‐2‐like protein, the GSH1 gene, which is involved in the biosynthesis of γ‐glutamate cysteine synthetases and the CSD3 protein, which plays a role in chitin synthesis and/or regulation.

the sequence of the 37·5 kilobase region of yeast chromosome XI includes the SME1 gene and the CSD3, GSH1, MEF1 and TCP‐1 genes, an open reading frames similar to the DAL8 gene, a tRNAArg and a gene with unknown function.
the complete sequence of the yeast chromosome X cosmid clone pYAC59 has been determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the complete nucleotide sequence of the yeast chromosome X region between the centromere and the telomere.
the complete DNA sequence of a 37·5 kilobase region on the left arm of yeast chromosome X.

the complete nucleotide sequence of a 37·5‐kb region of yeast chromosome XI, which includes the SME1, MEF2, GSH1 and the CSD3 genes as well as an ORF similar to DAL80, an ORF related to a TCP‐1 chaperonin, an ORF homologous to three regions of the DAL8 gene and a tRNA Arg3 (AGC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sequence contains at least 11 genes or ORFs with unknown functions.
the sequence of p59 represents a 37.5 kb segment of yeast chromosome X.
the sequence contains at least 15 genes, 14 of which are already known, and that it is located in the middle of chromosome X.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sequence of the 37·5 kbp of yeast chromosome X presented here is a typical example for the complexity of eukaryotic genomes.
the region of chromosome X contains genes encoding a putative chaperonin, a negative regulator of amino acid biosynthesis, and a γ‐glutamate‐cysteine ligase, as well as genes with unknown function.
the region contains a total of 16 genes and 14 ORFs, 11 of which represent new genes or ORFs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sequence of a 37.5-kilobase (kb) region of the yeast chromosome X contains 14 open-reading frames (ORFs).
there are many genes that are not essential for yeast growth in rich media but that are essential for yeast growth under stress.
the yeast genome contains many genes with homology to the DAL80 and TCP‐1 genes.
